anomalies.obs: On the CM4 sheet, the SN74LVC1G07-type buffer U2 is inserted in the power-enable path: its output Y (pin 4) feeds SW1 pin 1, SW1 pin 2 carries GLOBAL_EN to Module1 pin 99. U2's input A (pin 1) is tied to GND and its /OE (pin 3) is also tied to GND, so the open-drain output Y can never sink or source — it is permanently high-Z. Worse, the CM4's RUN_PG output (Module1 pin 25) is wired to U2 pin 2, which on this part is the chip's GND pin, so RUN_PG drives a floating ground pin instead of being used or terminated.
anomalies.exp: The specification states the intended design has GLOBAL_EN 'tied directly to SW1 pin 2' and that 'there is currently no delay/sequencing IC on this net, only a direct switch connection' — i.e. closing SW1 should pull GLOBAL_EN high to enable the CM4. No buffer should sit between the switch and GLOBAL_EN, and RUN_PG should not be connected to a buffer's GND pin.

evidence.quote: CM4 sheet: U2 pin 2 = RUN_PG (from Module1 pin 25), pin 1 = GND, pin 3 (/OE) = GND, pin 4 Y = SW1.1; SW1.2 = GLOBAL_EN = Module1 pin 99 (GLOBAL_EN)
GLOBAL_EN net, tied directly to SW1 pin 2 ... the netlist confirms there is currently no delay/sequencing IC on this net, only a direct switch connection.

anomalies.impact: With U2's A and /OE both at GND, Y is always high-Z, so closing SW1 leaves GLOBAL_EN floating and the CM4 can never be power-enabled; the rover will not boot. The RUN_PG output is also misconnected to U2's ground pin, leaving the CM4 power-good signal unused/mis-driven.

parsed.summary: The build deviates from the specified direct-switch GLOBAL_EN power-enable path: a buffer U2 is inserted with its input and /OE both tied to GND (output permanently high-Z), so the enable switch can never assert GLOBAL_EN, and RUN_PG is miswired to U2's ground pin. Other checked items (16 MHz crystals Y1/Y2, MCP2515 CAN controllers, SM712 TVS arrays, LTC4412 USB ideal-diode, e-stop sink buffers) match the specification.
